ai.title: General agent adds context-pruner and loops steps
ai.summary: General agent now runs `context-pruner` before each step via `spawn_agent_inline` and loops until `stepsComplete`. Prompts clarify lack of conversation history, requiring explicit context in `prompt` or `filePaths`. `instructionsPrompt` tightened to focus on parallel spawning. Scope limited to `agents/general-agent/general-agent.ts`.

eli5.text: The general-purpose AI agent now clears out old, irrelevant information from its memory before it starts thinking, so it doesn't get distracted or confused by details that no longer matter. It also works in a loop, taking focused steps until your task is complete rather than rushing through everything at once. You'd notice this when you ask the agent to help with something complex: it will keep working methodically, trimming unnecessary context along the way, instead of getting lost or giving up halfway. This change is live today and applies to anyone using the general-purpose agent.

ai.title: context-pruner captures strreplace and writefile diffs
ai.summary: Context pruner now includes diff results from `str_replace` and `write_file` tool messages in its summary. This ensures the agent retains visibility of file changes made during execution. The logic truncates diffs exceeding 2000 characters to manage context window size. Implemented in `agents/context-pruner.ts`.

eli5.text: When the assistant edits a file using the text-replacement tool or saves a new copy of a file, those edits now show up in the running summary that tracks what the assistant has done so far. You’d see a short note labeled [EDIT RESULT] or [WRITE RESULT] with the actual before-and-after text of the change, trimmed to about 2,000 characters so the record stays readable. The change went live today, affecting anyone who lets the assistant make and later review its file edits.

ai.title: CLI updates terminal title per user input
ai.summary: The CLI now sets the terminal window title to the user's current input, prefixed with 'Codebuff: '. This uses OSC escape sequences written directly to `/dev/tty` to bypass OpenTUI's stdout capture. Titles are truncated to 60 characters and sanitized. The title resets to default on exit via `renderer-cleanup.ts`. tmux and screen passthrough are handled automatically.

eli5.text: When you type a prompt into Codebuff in your terminal, your terminal window's title bar now shows your prompt instead of the default title. The title is prefixed with 'Codebuff: ' and truncated to keep it readable. This works even if you're using tmux or screen terminal multiplexers, and the title resets to its default when you exit.

ai.title: Add OSC52 clipboard support to CLI
ai.summary: Added OSC52 escape sequence support to `cli/src/utils/clipboard.ts` for cross-platform clipboard copying, particularly over SSH or headless environments. The implementation attempts OSC52 first, falling back to platform-specific tools (`pbcopy`, `xclip`, `xsel`, `clip`) if it fails. Includes handling for tmux and GNU screen passthrough wrapping, with a 32KB payload limit.

eli5.text: When you copy something to your clipboard while working through a secure remote connection (like logging into another computer), it now works reliably instead of failing silently. The system first tries a modern terminal method that travels over the connection, and if that doesn't work, it falls back to the classic copy commands your computer already uses. If you're a developer copying text in a terminal session, especially over SSH or in a headless environment, you'll notice the clipboard actually receives your copied content instead of the operation failing. This fix is live now.

ai.title: Release 1.0.598 adds terminal title, OSC52 clipboard, and FREE mode
ai.summary: Freebuff ships 1.0.598 bundling same-day commits that set the terminal window title to user input via OSC sequences to /dev/tty (truncated to 60 chars, with tmux/screen passthrough), add OSC52 clipboard support in cli/src/utils/clipboard.ts (32KB payload limit, falling back to pbcopy/xclip/xsel/clip), and introduce FREE mode replacing LITE via base2-free.ts with hardcoded ads on and zero-credit allowlisted combos mapped through AGENT_MODE_TO_COST_MODE. The general agent now runs context-pruner before each step via spawn_agent_inline looping until stepsComplete, researcher-docs and researcher-web switch to x-ai/grok-4.1-fast, docs and web search endpoints hardcode zero credits, chat history load caps at 500 entries skipping empty chats, and fallback commander-to-commander-lite logic lives in packages/agent-runtime/tool-executor.ts.
ai.evidence: cli/release/package.json hunk changes version from 1.0.597 to 1.0.598; analysis notes classify commit as release-bump with version-bump category, and surrounding same-day commits cover general-agent context-pruner, CLI terminal title, OSC52 clipboard, researcher model changes, FREE mode replacing LITE, and zero-credit docs/web search.

eli5.text: This update brings a smarter research experience, a cleaner terminal interface, and expanded free access to powerful AI agents. You can now use the web and document researcher agents at no cost, and they run on an upgraded model (grok-4.1-fast) for faster, better research results. The program now shows your current typing as the terminal window title, and you can copy text even when connected remotely over SSH. Chat history loading is faster and skips empty conversations, and the context-aware coding agent now automatically trims irrelevant background details to focus on what you need. Overall, you get more capable research tools for free, a more polished terminal experience, and smoother coding sessions.

ai.title: CLI routes terminal detection through getCliEnv
ai.summary: Clipboard OSC52 sequences and terminal title builders now read TERM, TMUX, and STY via getCliEnv instead of direct process.env access. This fixes process.env enforcement errors by centralizing terminal detection variables in CliEnv type and utils/env.ts. Scope limited to CLI core: types/env.ts, utils/clipboard.ts, utils/env.ts, utils/terminal-title.ts. tmux/screen DCS passthrough logic remains unchanged, only the variable source shifts.

eli5.text: When you copy something to the clipboard or update your terminal window title, the program now checks your terminal type by reading three specific settings (TERM, TMUX, and STY) from a single shared place instead of looking them up individually each time. This only affects the command-line tool's interaction with your terminal: nothing about what gets copied or displayed changes, just that the check happens consistently in one spot. The behavior is live today for anyone using the CLI to manage clipboard contents or terminal titles in tmux or screen sessions.

ai.title: GLM 4.7 editor added for Lite mode
ai.summary: New `editor-glm` agent definition added to `agents/editor/editor-glm.ts`, replacing `editor-gpt-5` in Lite mode. `createCodeEditor` in `agents/editor/editor.ts` updated to accept `'glm'` model option, mapping to `z-ai/glm-4.7`. `agents/base2/base2.ts` updated to spawn `editor-glm` instead of `editor-gpt-5` for Lite mode prompts. GLM and GPT-5 models skip `<think>` tag prompting in editor instructions.

eli5.text: When you use the Lite version of the assistant to help write code, it will now ask a different AI helper to do the typing for it. That helper has switched from one provider to a newer one called GLM 4.7. The only thing you might notice is that the code suggestions could come back slightly faster or phrased a bit differently than before.

ai.title: GPT-5 general agent omits file-picker
ai.summary: GPT-5 general agent excludes `file-picker` from `spawnableAgents` and drops related guidance from `instructionsPrompt`. Prevents repeated full-file reads by GPT-5. Scoped to `agents/general-agent/general-agent.ts` via conditional `buildArray` logic.

eli5.text: The GPT-5 general agent can no longer use a helper called file-picker that finds relevant files, because that helper reads every file it returns in full each time it runs, which slows things down. If you interact with the GPT-5 general agent now, you will simply not see file-picker as one of the available helpers it can call, and it will skip any instructions that mention using it. This only affects the GPT-5 version of the general agent; other versions keep file-picker.

ai.title: Refine askuser guidance in base2 agent
ai.summary: Updated prompt instructions for the `ask_user` tool in `agents/base2/base2.ts`. The guidance now explicitly restricts usage to non-obvious choices, removing ambiguity about when to skip the step. This change applies to the base2 agent configuration.

eli5.text: The base2 agent will now ask you a clarifying question before starting work only when there's a real choice to make and the best path isn't clear. When the right approach is obvious, it just proceeds without interrupting you. This makes interactions feel less chatty and more focused on the important decisions.

ai.title: CLI handles native reasoning blocks in agent streams
ai.summary: CLI now parses native reasoning chunks for agent blocks instead of relying solely on think tag parsing. `block-operations.ts` adds `appendNativeReasoningToBlocks` and `closeNativeReasoningBlock` to manage `textType: 'reasoning'` states, while `stream-chunk-processor.ts` propagates `textType` to agent destinations. `sdk-event-handlers.ts` ensures reasoning blocks close before tool calls execute.

eli5.text: When an AI agent in the command line shows its step-by-step thinking before acting, that thinking display now appears correctly and disappears cleanly once the agent moves on to doing work. Previously, the thinking text could get stuck looking like it was still being written, even after the agent had finished. Now, if the agent jumps straight from thinking to taking an action like running a tool, the thinking section properly closes instead of lingering on screen.

ai.title: openai-compatible generate missing tool call id
ai.summary: openai-compatible-chat-language-model.ts generates missing tool call IDs via generateId() instead of throwing InvalidResponseDataError. Handles providers like GLM omitting IDs in streaming deltas. Internal package fix, no user-facing surface change.

eli5.text: Some providers that supply a conversational helper were sending along a tracking label with each suggested action but occasionally forgetting to include the unique reference number that labels are supposed to carry. Previously the system treated that missing number as a hard error and would stop the response mid-stream. Now, when a provider omits the number, the system simply generates a temporary one on the fly so the response keeps flowing instead of breaking. You wouldn't notice a difference unless you were already running into the spot where the response used to cut off, and then you'd just see it complete normally rather than stop.

ai.title: Remove readsubtree from file-lister agent
ai.summary: File-lister agent in agents/file-explorer/file-lister.ts no longer uses the read_subtree tool. The toolNames array is cleared, preventing the agent from traversing the filesystem subtree. This change restricts the file-lister's capabilities to its core listing function.

eli5.text: If you asked this helper to go dig through every folder and file on your computer, it can no longer do that. The change took away the helper's ability to look deep into your file system, so it's now limited to simply listing files at the top level. It affects anyone who relied on this helper's deeper exploration feature, which no longer works.

ai.title: FREE mode replaces LITE, forces ads, zero-cost billing
ai.summary: CLI and agent runtime introduce FREE mode, replacing LITE. `base2-free.ts` spawns `commander-lite` and `editor-glm` via `x-ai/grok-4.1-fast`. `--lite` flag deprecated in favor of `--free`. `getAdsEnabled` hardcodes `true` for FREE mode; `use-gravity-ad` sends mode to API to block credit grants. `AGENT_MODE_TO_COST_MODE` maps FREE to 'free' cost mode, passing `costMode` to `createRunConfig` for zero-credit allowlisted combos. Thinking block completion logic simplified in `thinking-block.tsx` and `message-updater.ts` to auto-collapse native reasoning on message end.

eli5.text: If you run the CLI in the free tier today, it now calls the free orchestrator instead of the lite one, serves you ads without asking, and tells the billing API you're on a free plan so it won't grant you credits. The old --lite flag no longer exists; use --free instead. You'll see the thinking/reasoning block collapse automatically once your message finishes streaming, and the terminal title updates as you type. This rolled out with release 1.0.598.

ai.title: CLI release version bumped to 1.0.599
ai.summary: Version 1.0.599 is a routine release increment that rolls up the day's user-facing changes into the CLI package manifest. The bump follows terminal-detection centralization through getCliEnv, the new GLM 4.7 editor for Lite mode replacing editor-gpt-5, GPT-5 general agent omitting file-picker, refined ask_user guidance in base2, CLI native reasoning block parsing, the openai-compatible tool call ID fix, read_subtree removal from file-lister, and the FREE mode replacing LITE with forced ads and zero-cost billing. No new code ships in this commit; the version field is the only change.
ai.evidence: Version field in `cli/release/package.json` updated from 1.0.598 to 1.0.599, a single-line bump with no other file changes in this commit.

eli5.text: This release introduces FREE mode, which replaces the old LITE mode and lets you use the tool at no cost while showing you relevant ads to support the service. You can now use a new AI model, GLM 4.7, as your code editor in FREE mode, which replaces GPT-5 for that role. The tool now reads your terminal information more reliably, so features like copying text and setting window titles work better across different terminal setups. The agent now handles reasoning steps more clearly, so you can follow along with its thinking process as it works through tasks before jumping into actions. GPT-5 general tasks now skip repeatedly reading whole files, so they finish faster and use less of your time. Overall, upgrading gives you a free tier with a capable AI editor, smoother terminal integration, and a more transparent agent that explains its reasoning before acting.
